record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: For a pseudo-oval O(n, n, q) over a field of odd order q, must O always be classical, meaning a classical pseudo-oval in the sense used in the paper?

evidence.quote: 4. Is any O(n, n, q), q odd, always classical?
For n = m such a set O(n, n, q) is called a pseudo-oval or a generalized oval or an [n − 1]-oval of PG(3n − 1, q).

A regular pseudo-oval for which O1 is a conic is called either a pseudo-conic or a classical pseudo-oval, and a regular pseudo-ovoid for which O1 is an elliptic quadric is called a pseudo-quadric or a classical pseudo-ovoid or a classical egg.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be an odd prime power and let $n\ge 1$ be an integer. Work in the projective space $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. A pseudo-oval $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}(n,n,q)$ is a family of $q^n+1$ pairwise disjoint $(n-1)$-dimensional projective subspaces of $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ such that any three of them span $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$. Equivalently, every $(n-1)$-space of $\mathcal{O}$ is contained in a unique tangent $(2n-1)$-space which meets no other element of $\mathcal{O}$. The pseudo-oval is called elementary (or arises from an oval) if there exist a field extension $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}/\mathbb{F}_q$, an embedding of $\mathrm{PG}(2,q^n)$ as a spread-induced structure in $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$, and an oval (a set of $q^n+1$ points, no three collinear) $\mathcal{O}_1\subset \mathrm{PG}(2,q^n)$ whose points correspond to the $(n-1)$-spaces of $\mathcal{O}$. A pseudo-oval is called classical (or a pseudo-conic) if it is elementary and $\mathcal{O}_1$ can be chosen to be a non-degenerate conic in $\mathrm{PG}(2,q^n)$.

Question: For every odd prime power $q$ and every integer $n\ge 1$, must every pseudo-oval $\mathcal{O}(n,n,q)$ in $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ be classical?
artifact.status_search_result: The classicality of pseudo-ovals $\mathcal{O}(n,n,q)$ for odd $q$ appears to remain an open problem in finite geometry. Recent (2024) classification work establishes classicality only in small/special cases (e.g. small orders, or when an associated projective plane is Desarguesian), but no general resolution for arbitrary odd $q$ and arbitrary $n$ has been found.

status_evidence.title: Classifying pseudo-ovals, translation generalized quadrangles, and elation Laguerre planes of small order
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of pseudo-ovals in PG(3n-1,q) for n=5,6 with a Desarguesian associated plane, and of TGQs of order ≤ 64; classicality known only in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, only partial classification results are known; general classicality for odd q remains unresolved.
